newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to invest 35 bln esc in airports by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to invest 35 bln esc in airports by 2000.

text.p: The Portuguese government plans to invest 35.2 billion escudos to improve the airports of Lisbon, Oporto and Faro by the year 2000, Public Works Minister Joao Cravinho said.
Most of the funds will be invested to upgrade Lisbon airport, including restructuring entrances and exits and building a car park, Cravinho told reporters.
The investments are needed because the airports are facing increasing demand as the century draws to a close, he said.

Cravinho said that despite the planned investments, Lisbon airport would be operating at full capacity between 2003 and 2007, justifying the construction of a second airport to serve the capital, which is expected to be operational from 2007.
He said the investments would include eight billion escudos to upgrade Faro airport and 6.6 billion to improve Oporto airport.
